Home.storyTitle: Claudya's first trip to Pulaski changed everything.
Home.storyBody: Three years ago, a trip to the Salmon River in Pulaski, New York, turned Claudya into a fly angler for good. Two years ago, she picked up a vise. This season, tying got serious — patterns built for the species she actually chases: walleye, bass, pike, and the steelhead and salmon that started it all. And there's a next generation already curious about all of it, which is the part we didn't plan on.
Home.valuesHandmadeBody: No mass production — every fly is checked before it ships.
Home.valuesLocalBody: Patterns designed for our rivers, our lakes, and our seasons.
Home.valuesQualityBody: Every pattern gets fished before it gets sold — not just tied to look right in the box.
Home.newsletterBody: New patterns, seasonal picks, and notes from the vise — straight to your inbox.

About.title: Started on the Salmon River, tied on our own bench.
About.metaDescription: La Moucherie is a family bench in Montérégie, Québec, run by Claudya and Kevin — hand-tied flies, tested on the water they're tied for, sold the way we'd want to buy them ourselves.
About.p1: La Moucherie is run by Claudya Cazes and Kevin — she ties, he keeps the shop running, and between the two of us there's rarely a day without a fly in the vise. Claudya's own path to fly fishing started three years ago, on a trip to Pulaski, New York — the kind of first trip that changes what you fish for good. She fell for it standing in that river, and she's been chasing that feeling ever since, on the fly rod and off it: walleye, bass, pike, whatever's biting, spinning or baitcast when the fly rod isn't the right tool for the day.
About.p2: Two years ago, tying flies together became part of that — something to do at the bench between trips, tying to the species and water she actually fishes rather than a stock catalog. This season it turned into something more serious and more careful: patterns tested on the same water they're tied for, sized and weighted for how she actually fishes them, sold the way we'd want to buy them ourselves.
About.p3: We're small on purpose. Every fly that leaves this bench has been tied by one of us, checked by the other, and packed by hand — no factory bin, no minimum order neither of us would want to fill.
About.quote: My first trip to Pulaski changed what I fish for — three years later, I'm tying the flies myself. — Claudya
About.p4: Family business is a phrase that gets used loosely, so here is what we mean by it: two of us at one bench, and a next generation already taken with fishing — no encouragement required. We would rather build something worth handing down than something worth scaling.

FAQ.title: Frequently asked questions
FAQ.intro: Shipping, sizes, returns, custom patterns — the questions we get most.
FAQ.q1: Are your flies tied in Québec?
FAQ.a1: Yes, every fly is hand-tied at our bench in Montérégie, Québec.
FAQ.a3: Letter mail starts at {letterPrice} for a small order; tracked parcel shipping is free once your order reaches {threshold}.
FAQ.q4: How long does an order take?
FAQ.a4: Orders are tied and packed by hand and go out within 2–5 business days.
FAQ.q5: What hook sizes do you carry?
FAQ.a5: It varies by pattern — each product page lists the exact sizes currently available.
FAQ.a6: If a fly isn't right, write to us within 30 days and we'll replace it or refund it. Flies that have already been fished can't be returned.
FAQ.q7: Can I request a custom pattern?
FAQ.a7: Yes — tell us what you're after through the contact page and we'll let you know if we can tie it.
FAQ.q8: How should I store my flies?
FAQ.a8: Somewhere dry, out of direct sun — a standard fly box works fine. Let flies dry fully before boxing them after a day on the water, to keep hooks from rusting.
FAQ.q9: Do you work with fly shops, guides, or outfitters?
FAQ.a9: Yes — see our wholesale page for details.

Hatches.metaTitle: Southern Québec Hatch Chart — La Moucherie
Hatches.metaDescription: A month-by-month hatch chart for southern Québec rivers: mayflies, caddis, stoneflies, midges and terrestrials, with emergence windows, hook sizes, time of day and the patterns that match each one.
Hatches.title: Southern Québec hatch chart
Hatches.intro: What emerges, when, and what to tie on. Built for the rivers we fish in the Laurentides, l'Estrie and the Montérégie — emergence windows, hook sizes, time of day, and the pattern that covers each hatch.
Hatches.disclaimer: Hatches follow water temperature, not the calendar: a cold spring pushes everything back a week or two, a warm one pulls it forward. Treat every window as ±10 days and trust a stream thermometer over this chart. It is a seasonal reference, not a live conditions report.
